newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli stocks mixed ahead of rate announcement.
newsitem.headline: Israeli stocks mixed ahead of rate announcement.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed mixed with a positive bias on Sunday as investors remained sidelined ahead of the Bank of Israel's announcement on its key interest rate on Monday, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.12 percent, or 0.24 points, to 198.21 on all-share turnover of 66 million shekels against 77 million on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.18 percent to 207.90.

"Trading was mixed and selective. The market is waiting for the central bank's decision on interest rates. Investors expect it (the central bank) will lower the rates by 0.2-0.3 percentage points," said Shar Gazit at Batucha Securities.

Clal Electronic Industries surged 4.0 percent to 26,634 but traders said there was no evident reason for the sharp rise. The company will hold a news conference on Monday but Clal officials refused to comment on what will be announced.
"After a few weeks of nice gains we saw some profit taking today. The market remained stable as investors wait for the interest rate decision," said one trader.

"The market is expecting a moderate rate cut of around 0.3 percentage points. Most investors prefer to wait and see what will happen with the interest rate," he added. The central bank's key short-term lending rate is now at 15.2 percent.

The most active shares were Clal Industries, which rose 2.75 percent to 1,349 on volume of 3.5 million shekels; Elbit, which gained 2.0 percent to 14,918 on turnover of 3.4 million shekels; and Bank Hapoalim, which rose 1.5 percent to 483 on volume of 2.9 million shekels.
